title: Shelf-Stable Food Safety (Food Safety Information fact sheet, updated August 2014)
org: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS), via GovInfo
licence_note: US federal government work; FSIS encourages reprint (the PhotoDisc cover image is excluded). Read 2026-11-16 by R17 (GovInfo copy; fsis.usda.gov refuses automated fetch): dating is for quality, not safety, except infant formula; discard deeply dented cans (a dent you can lay a finger into) and any deep dent on a seam; small dent otherwise sound is safe; discard heavily rusted cans; discard swollen frozen cans and frozen cans thawed at 40 F or higher; below 85 F best, over 100 F harmful; chart: low-acid canned goods 2 to 5 years, high-acid 12 to 18 months; botulism warnings: leaking, bulging or badly dented cans, cracked jars, loose or bulging lids, foul odour, spurting.

title: Home-Canned Foods (Botulism: Prevention)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R17 via the fetch tool (curl gets 403): when in doubt, throw it out: container leaking, bulging or swollen; looks damaged, cracked or abnormal; spurts liquid or foam when opened; food discoloured, mouldy or smells bad. At altitudes below 1,000 feet, boil foods for 10 minutes; add 1 minute for each additional 1,000 feet.

title: Botulism: Signs and Symptoms
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R17 via the fetch tool: difficulty swallowing, muscle weakness, double vision, drooping eyelids, blurry vision, slurred speech, difficulty breathing, difficulty moving the eyes.

title: Healthy Habits: Antibiotic Do's and Don'ts
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R17 via the fetch tool: take antibiotics only when you need them; antibiotics do not work on viruses (colds, flu); do not share your antibiotics; do not take antibiotics prescribed for someone else; side effects include C. diff diarrhoea and severe allergic reactions; use contributes to resistance.

title: Guidelines for Children's Agricultural Tasks Demonstrate Effectiveness (NIOSH Publication 2011-129, March 2011)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R17 on archive.cdc.gov via the fetch tool (live cdc.gov copy 404/403): NAGCAT, built on child-development principles, matched a child's physical, mental and psychosocial abilities with the requirements of specific farm work, to help parents assign farm work appropriately.

title: Chainsaw Safety QuickCard (OSHA 3269)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R17: proper personal protective equipment must be worn when operating the saw: hand, foot, leg, eye, face, hearing and head protection. (Replaces the dead URL on osha-chain-saw-safety-protective-equipment-for-chain-a71d7d.)

title: Hand and Power Tools (OSHA 3080, 2002 revised)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R17: employees should be trained in the proper use of all tools; appropriate personal protective equipment such as safety goggles and gloves.

title: Guidance: Potassium Iodide as a Thyroid Blocking Agent in Radiation Emergencies (December 2001), PDF
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R17 (the archived copy of us-fda-potassium-iodide-as-a-thyroid-blocking-agent-fcadee holds no text): adults over 40 need take KI only in the case of a projected large internal radiation dose to the thyroid (>500 cGy) to prevent hypothyroidism; iodine-induced thyrotoxicosis is more common in older people and in iodine-deficient areas but usually requires repeated doses.
